_comment: P-TQA.7 — accepted/pre-existing high+critical advisories. The audit gate (scripts/auditGate.mjs) BLOCKS any high/critical NOT listed here. Each entry is triaged: dev-only, no safe fix, or a separate upgrade task. Re-triage periodically and remove once fixed. A NEW high/critical in any other package fails CI. Since 2026-10-04 (Q-619) an entry accepts ONLY the high/critical advisory ids in its advisories list: a new advisory in an allowlisted package blocks until it is triaged and its id added. An entry vulnerable only through another package lists none; that advisory is judged on its own package.

GHSA (RSC-mode CSRF bypass, range >=7.12.0 <8.3.0) applies ONLY to React Router's RSC/server-action mode; NavBharatAI is a Vite SPA using client-side routing (no RSC), so it is not exploitable. The only npm 'fix' is a breaking v8 major (>=8.3.0) or a downgrade to <7.12.0 which REINTRODUCES the 7.18.0-patched DoS (GHSA-chx6-hx7r-mcp5). Pinned at 7.18.1 (DoS-patched); v8 migration tracked separately.
Same advisory as react-router (via react-router). RSC-mode-only CSRF, not applicable to our SPA. Pinned at 7.18.1 (DoS-patched); v8 upgrade is a breaking major, tracked separately.

GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg (DoS via unbounded expansion), fixed only in 5.0.8. Root-caused and attempted a `package.json` overrides pin to 5.0.8 (2026-07-25) — reverted because 5.0.8 changed its CJS export shape and broke the legacy minimatch bundled inside glob (used by @vitest/coverage-v8's test-exclude → glob chain): `brace_expansion_1.default is not a function`, a real CI failure, not a hypothetical. Every reachable instance is transitive-only via dev/CLI tooling (firebase-tools, vitest coverage) — never imported in src/, never shipped, never run against user-supplied input (only against our own trusted repo paths/config globs). True fix needs glob's bundled minimatch (inside test-exclude/coverage-v8) and firebase-tools' vendored minimatch to publish a brace-expansion@5.x-compatible release; tracked as an open root cause, revisit periodically. RE-TRIAGED 2026-10-04 (Q-619) for GHSA-qhr7-859c-m2p7 and GHSA-6j4f-fj2g-mc7p — both NEWER than the advisory this entry was written for, and both had been passing under its package name unseen. Same reachability: every copy is transitive (firebase-tools CLI, vitest coverage, and exceljs → unzipper → fstream, whose glob-using writer exceljs never calls — it parses xlsx in memory). None expands a pattern a user supplies.

Same brace-expansion cascade (glob's bundled minimatch, and the copy vendored inside firebase-tools). Dev-only (firebase-tools CLI / vitest coverage), never shipped, never reachable by users. See brace-expansion entry above for the full root-cause note.
Same brace-expansion/minimatch cascade. Dev-only: only reached via firebase-tools (CLI) and test-exclude (vitest coverage tooling). Never shipped, never reachable by users.

Aggregates the brace-expansion/minimatch/glob cascade in its own dependency tree. devDependency only (the Firebase deploy CLI) — never imported in src/, never bundled into the shipped app or server. npm's suggested 'fix' is a downgrade to 14.23.0 (a semver-major regression, not an upgrade); the real fix is upstream (firebase-tools needs to update its vendored glob/minimatch to a brace-expansion@5.x-compatible version). Tracked as an open root cause.

GHSA-86w9-cpqp-85rv (RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature VERIFICATION accepts extra nested DigestAlgorithm elements); published 2026-10-04, no fixed release (<=1.4.0 is every release). Direct dependency used ONLY in src/server/lib/androidKeystore.ts to GENERATE a user's Android upload key: createCertificate + self-sign + PKCS#12 export. Nothing in the repo calls node-forge's signature verification, and no untrusted signature is ever handed to it, so the flawed path is unreachable. Re-triage when a fixed release exists. RE-TRIAGED 2026-10-04 (Q-619) for GHSA-86w9-cpqp-85rv (RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature VERIFICATION accepts malformed signatures; no fixed version exists): `androidKeystore.ts` only GENERATES and SERIALISES keystores with forge (keygen runs on Node's native crypto); no code verifies a signature with node-forge.

GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm (stack exhaustion on deeply nested patterns), published 2026-10-04; the advisory covers <=3.0.3 and 3.0.3 is the LATEST release, so no fix exists upstream. Reached only as firebase-tools -> chokidar@3 -> braces: a devDependency CLI (the Firebase deploy tool), never imported in src/, never shipped, never run against user-supplied patterns. Remove when chokidar@4 (no braces) reaches firebase-tools or braces publishes a fix. RE-TRIAGED 2026-10-04 (Q-619) for GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm: only via chokidar inside the firebase-tools CLI (dev/deploy tooling), never shipped, never fed user patterns.
Same braces advisory, via chokidar@3's dependency on braces (firebase-tools pins ^3.6.0 as of 15.32.1). Dev-only firebase-tools CLI, never shipped. See the braces entry.
